quarterly_data.quarter: TE Connectivity Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: First time management has given the AI ORDER rate: 'Our DDN orders are up 70%' this year while revenue grew about 30%, because those orders are for 2027 programs already won with hyperscaler customers for the copper connectivity on their GPU networks. That sets up a record backlog entering fiscal 2027, and the $3 billion cloud-and-AI target given at the Investor Day keeps 'shifting left' (management: 'that $3 billion shifted in, and that is going to continue to shift to the left').
quarterly_data.figure: DDN orders are up 70%; we grew $1 billion this year in DDN; $3 billion cloud-and-AI Investor Day target being pulled forward

quarterly_data.quarter: TE Connectivity Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Asked whether AI orders stretch out the way they do for supply-constrained component makers, the CEO said connectors are NOT tight: 'We don't have that supply tightness' — TE's order book runs typically into 2027 and 2028 orders should start arriving early in 2027, with engineering engagement on next-generation architectures (who goes 800V, liquid vs air cooling, where optics enters the rack) already running for 2028-2029. On capacity and moat: three new facilities added in Southeast Asia over the past three years for China plus one with more being added right now, and engineering headcount raised by about 2,500 people over three years; TE cites 448G speeds and signal integrity as the technical bar.
quarterly_data.figure: three new facilities in Southeast Asia over the past three years; engineering from 7,500 to about 10,000 (about 2,500 people added); 448G speeds

quarterly_data.quarter: TE Connectivity Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Optics positioning sharpened and the price of this year's optics technology acquisition disclosed: TE made a '$200 million acquisition earlier this year to help buffer the portfolio' in optics (the company is not named in this session). TE plays in scale-up and 'we do not play as much in the scale out'; it expects NPO and CPO to show up 'more at the switch level is where you are going to first see it', and its own entry is the fiber attach unit — 'essentially a fiber connector that would actually help enable CPO or NPO' — which is incremental TAM on top of the copper portfolio. The milestones to watch are the customer's architecture intercept point, engineering qualification, then scaling to AI/hyperscaler unit volumes.
quarterly_data.figure: $200 million acquisition earlier this year to buffer the optics portfolio

quarterly_data.quarter: TE Connectivity Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Quantified the data-center pull inside the energy business: energy is now a '$2 billion business' growing double digits, in a market 'probably growing 3x what it used to' (from 1%-2%), and management says 'About 30% of our business does come from' grid hardening plus getting the power to the data centers in North America. TE frames this as a second AI growth vector alongside the rack — 'not only what we do with the rack, but also getting the power to the data center'.
quarterly_data.figure: energy a $2 billion business growing double digits; About 30% of our business from grid hardening / power to the data centers; market growing 3x what it used to
